messages:
nate: Heads-up — since the late-night scheduler rollout we've seen a tiny but persistent wave of tiny-pod evictions in us-west1b. Looks correlated with warm-pool handoffs around AZ boundary.
priya: Saw that too. CPU/GPU pods getting Pending -> CrashLoopBackOff after a preempt. Eviction spikes ~2-3/min for the last 45m.
oliver: Any recent taint/affinity changes rolled? Or a nodepool scale event?
priya: No scale. Scheduler change was the only deploy (weighting tweak). No taint changes.
sre-bot: Alert: eviction-rate(us-west1b) > baseline by 6.8x for pods with gpu=true. Metric: eviction_count per 5m window.
maya: Quick snippet from node events:
```
Warning Preempted pod/worker-xyz Preempted by higher priority pod
Normal NodeLifecycle node/compute-az1 Drain completed
Warning Evicting pod/loader-abc eviction threshold exceeded
```
aj: Trying `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep Pending` — most stuck ones are tiny gpus (1/2 slot), with node affinity to az1.
priya: Hypothesis: warm-pool handoff code is serializing allocations across AZs; when pool in az1 is drained it tries to cold-start in az2 but latebind + affinity means tiny pods are shuffled and preempted repeatedly.
nate: Agree. Also seeing KV cache pressure on runtime side during the handoff window — could be causing long scheduling decisions, leading to leases timing out and preempt signals stacking.
oliver: Can we confirm with scheduler traces? I can pull the trace for the rollout window.
maya: Also cpu/memory on nodes are fine; it's specifically slot-granularity and preemption churn. Evicted pods often re-schedule to same AZ then evicted again.
priya: Short-term mitigation: increase warm-pool min size in us-west1b by +3 to absorb the handoff while we investigate. Also add a temporary preempt buffer (lower preempt threshold) for tiny pods.
aj: Will that require a nodepool change? I can submit a hot patch to autoscaler config.
nate: Go for it. aj please patch warm-pool min=+3 and set scheduler preempt_threshold to 0.85 for tiny-pod class. Rollback window 30m if no improvement.
oliver: Extracted scheduler trace: decision latency spikes at ~1200ms for tiny pods during handoff. Also see many `Predicate` retries indicating affinity mismatch attempts.
maya: Can we tweak preferNoSchedule to soft-enforce cross-az spill instead of strict affinity? Might reduce oscillation.
priya: Longer-term: add an AZ-aware coalescing step in handoff path so we avoid serial cold starts. Also consider reserve slots for tiny pods during rolling changes.
aj: Patch applied: warm-pool increased, preempt_threshold set. Monitoring window started.
sre-bot: Event: warm-pool min increased for us-west1b by +3 (aj). Preempt threshold adjusted.
priya: Initial telemetry: eviction rate dropped ~70% in first 10m. Pending tiny pods moving to Running instead of flapping.
aj: Keeping it for 1h then we plan a graceful rollback to assess.
nate: Action items:
- oliver: dig deeper into scheduler trace and confirm where the predicate retries originate (due to AZ affinity or slot fragmentation)
- priya: prototype AZ-coalescing handoff and a small test in staging
- aj: keep warm-pool bump for 1h, then step down by 1 each 10m while observing
- maya: capture node-level metrics (gRPC latency, KV cache pressure) for the handoff window
Everyone: thumbs-up if ok.
priya: +1
oliver: +1
maya: +1
aj: +1
nate: Thanks — will follow up in morning with a short postmortem and a proposed safe rollout for the scheduler weight change that includes the coalescing step.
